query: Why do goal achievement rates differ across departments?

per_column.name: primary_lever
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the strategic approach behind each goal, giving a strong new grouping axis to compare achievement rates across lever types. Values align well with descriptions (cost_optimization, customer_service, people_programs, marketing_sales all warranted).

per_column.name: goal_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Captures the outcome mechanism (satisfaction/revenue/efficiency/cost). Somewhat correlated with primary_lever but distinct enough to be useful. Values are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: goal_specificity
per_column.rationale: Whether a goal is quantified and has a baseline is a plausible driver of achievement and a genuine new axis. Samples correctly distinguish 'from 78% to 90%' (with baseline) vs 'by 20%' (no baseline).

per_column.name: initiative_complexity
per_column.rationale: Multi vs single action vs program-level is a reasonable complexity axis that could explain differing achievement. Sample readings are defensible (multiple stated actions -> multi_action; 'comprehensive Program' -> program_level).

per_column.name: time_horizon
per_column.rationale: Deadline horizon is a strong explanatory variable for achievement rates. Extractions match text ('by end of Q4', 'next fiscal year', 'last quarter'). NULLs for silent rows are acceptable.

per_column.name: measurement_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Useful axis, but appears partly inferred from goal type rather than the actual metric column, which is often mismatched (e.g. metric 'Expense Ratio' on a customer-satisfaction goal was tagged survey_based). This inference is reasonable but occasionally overrides stated metric, introducing mild groundedness risk.

per_column.name: metric_goal_alignment
per_column.rationale: Whether the tracked metric fits the goal is directly relevant to why achievement differs and is well-grounded given metric vs description (e.g. Survey Score metric on a revenue goal -> false; Expense Ratio on cost reduction -> true).

per_column.name: scope_breadth
per_column.rationale: Conceptually useful, but heavily skewed to company_wide (428/550) and the sample labels several clearly department/team-scoped goals (satisfaction ratings, premium subscriptions) as company_wide. This suggests a default overreach not warranted by the text.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply several genuinely distinct, analytically valuable axes (lever, mechanism, specificity, complexity, time horizon, metric alignment) directly relevant to explaining cross-department achievement differences, with little trivial redundancy. Most values are sound readings of the source text. Groundedness is dragged down modestly by scope_breadth's over-assignment to company_wide and measurement_mechanism occasionally inferring from goal type over the stated metric, but reasonable NULL handling and generally faithful extractions keep overall quality high.
